mcq.e: ADSC (ADc Start Conversion); it clears when the conversion is done.

ADPS2..0 = 111 gives an ADC clock of (F_CPU = 16 MHz):
Why use a prescaler of 128 at 16 MHz?
o: To keep the ADC clock within about 50 to 200 kHz for full accuracy

mcq.q: ADLAR = 1 means:
o: Result left justified so ADCH holds the top 8 bits

mcq.q: ADCW provides:
o: A 16-bit access to the 10-bit result with six leading zeros

mcq.q: float vIn = ADCW * 5 / 1024; (all integers) gives a wrong result because:
o: Integer arithmetic: 5/1024 style truncation loses the fraction
mcq.e: Use 5.0 so the calculation is floating point.

mcq.q: Which vector is used for the ADC-complete interrupt?
In the interrupt voltmeter, the ISR must end by:
o: Restarting the conversion by setting ADSC
mcq.e: The ADC does not retrigger itself unless auto trigger is used.

mcq.e: Vin = V×R2/(R1+R2); small R1 gives Vin near 5 V.

o: The sensor output is small, so a smaller interval gives finer temperature resolution (about 0.1 °C)

mcq.q: To switch a 230 V lamp from a microcontroller pin you use:
o: A transistor-driven relay with a flyback diode, with proper isolation
mcq.e: Mains work needs qualified supervision and correct isolation.

mcq.q: The flyback diode across a relay coil:
o: Absorbs the voltage spike when the coil de-energises
mcq.e: Protects the transistor and the microcontroller.

mcq.q: A 4-bit successive-approximation ADC with Vref = 5 V converts 3 V. The result is...
Why does a 12-bit ADC take longer than an 8-bit one?
o: Successive approximation needs one compare step per bit
mcq.e: Each bit costs one compare cycle: more bits, more accuracy, more time.

mcq.q: ADCW is...
o: A hardware register listed in the datasheet
A virtual 16-bit register provided by the C compiler combining ADCL and ADCH
mcq.e: The chip is 8-bit; the compiler combines ADCL and ADCH. In assembly read ADCL and ADCH.

mcq.q: A sensor outputs 0-1 V. For best accuracy choose...
mcq.e: Step 1.07 mV instead of 4.88 mV, so small changes (e.g. 501 to 503 mV) become different numbers.

mcq.q: Why not use one shared resistor for 5 LEDs?
o: It may carry the sum of currents (e.g. 45 mA) and burn, and LEDs draw different currents
mcq.e: Use one resistor per LED, or a resistor array.

mcq.q: What does analogRead() use internally to wait for the result?
mcq.e: analogRead polls ADSC with a fixed /128 prescaler; Arduino has no ADC-interrupt wrapper.

written.q: Explain how a 10-bit ADC with Vref = 5 V converts 3.3 V and compute its resolution in volts. How can the accuracy be improved?
written.a: Interval size = 5/1024 = 4.883 mV; ADCW = floor(3.3 / 4.883 mV) = floor(675.84) = 675 (binary 1010100011, found by successive approximation: each of the 10 steps compares Vin with a DAC trial voltage). Reconstructed Vin = 675 × 5/1024 = 3.296 V. Accuracy improves with a higher resolution or a smaller Vref (for example the internal 1.1 V reference gives 1.07 mV per step for signals below 1.1 V).

written.q: List the steps and register settings to read channel ADC0 with Vref = AVcc in C and write the code to read the value in a loop.
written.a:
DDRC &= ~(1<<DDC0);
ADMUX = (ADMUX & ~(1<<REFS1)) | (1<<REFS0);   // Vref = AVcc
ADMUX &= ~((1<<MUX3)|(1<<MUX2)|(1<<MUX1)|(1<<MUX0)); // ADC0
ADCSRA |= (1<<ADPS2)|(1<<ADPS1)|(1<<ADPS0);       // /128 = 125 kHz
ADCSRA |= (1<<ADEN);
while(1){ ADCSRA |= (1<<ADSC); while(ADCSRA & (1<<ADSC)); v = ADCW; }

written.q: Design an LM35-based thermometer that switches on an LED above 30 °C. Compute the ADC threshold and the resolution for 5 V and 1.1 V references.
written.a: LM35 to A0 (+V to 5 V, GND to GND), LED with 220 Ω on pin 8. 30 °C = 0.30 V. With Vref = 5 V: threshold = 0.30/5 × 1024 = 61.4 (about 62), resolution 4.88 mV = 0.49 °C. With Vref = 1.1 V: threshold = 0.30/1.1 × 1024 = 279, resolution 1.07 mV = 0.107 °C, so the 1.1 V reference is better. Code: analogReference(INTERNAL); float t = analogRead(A0)*1.1/1024*100; digitalWrite(8, t > 30);

written.q: Compare the polling and interrupt-driven voltmeter implementations.
written.a: Polling: after setting ADSC the CPU waits in while (ADCSRA & (1<<ADSC)), so it is tied up for about 104 µs every conversion. Interrupt: enable ADIE and sei(), start once, and the ISR(ADC_vect) computes the voltage, sets the LEDs and restarts the ADC; main() is free for other work.

written.q: Explain successive approximation using a 4-bit ADC with Vin = 3 V and Vref = 5 V.
written.a: Guess Vref/2 = 2.5 V: Vin is higher, bit = 1, next guess 2.5 + 5/4 = 3.75 V. 3 < 3.75, bit 0, next 3.75 − 5/8 = 3.125 V. 3 < 3.125, bit 0, next 3.125 − 5/16 = 2.8125 V. 3 > 2.8125, bit 1. Result 1001 = 9. Each comparison gives one bit, stored in the data register.

written.q: Derive the formula Vin = ADC × Vref / 1024 and state the smallest change the ATmega328P ADC can detect with Vref = 5 V and 1.1 V.
written.a: 0 to Vref maps onto 0-1023, i.e. 1024 steps, so step size = Vref / 1024 and Vin = number of steps × step size. Smallest detectable change = one step: 5/1024 = 4.88 mV; 1.1/1024 = 1.07 mV.
